mobile_ap.executive_summary: Qualcomm is decisively shifting competitive leverage from process node density to architectural modularity and AI-native software stacks, with tangible moves to diversify away from TSMC: evaluating Samsung's 2nm process for flagship Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Extreme and broadening Snapdragon's IP surface across wearables, PCs (Linux), and personal AI devices via 1-bit model integration. This represents a material tightening of Qualcomm's customer lock-in at the software/ISA level while hedging foundry risk, whereas MediaTek's Dimensity 9600 Pro adoption of 2nm largely mirrors rather than innovates the node transition.

custom_soc.executive_summary: Custom SoC ordering acceleration continues across cloud hyperscalers (Amazon $25B silicon push, Google orbital AI test, SEMIFIVE's $52M contract win), with Broadcom consolidating market position as primary systems integrator outside the GPU cartel. Design automation tools (AI chip design in 2 weeks, MIPS-Xcelsa verification collaboration, proteanTecs monitoring) are lowering barriers to entry, but hyperscalers remain bottlenecked by capacity constraints and geopolitical risk (Broadcom China probe) rather than design capability.

foundry.executive_summary: TSMC solidifies capacity leadership through 1.4nm mass-production planning (late 2028) and price power via 3–6% 2027 wafer hikes, while Samsung gains traction as Qualcomm evaluates 2nm for Snapdragon. The competitive axis shifts toward multi-foundry hedging at advanced nodes, with interface risk moving from pure node scaling to differentiated packaging (Samsung's FC-BGA server substrate expansion, 4.27T₩ investment through May 2028) and ecosystem integration (SK Hynesis at TSMC OIP, Qualcomm's 2nm qualification pathway).

packaging.executive_summary: TSMC is executing a material capacity build-out, committing to 5 additional advanced packaging plants in Chiayi plus a Taichung hub in response to AI demand surge, while concurrently rallying domestic Taiwan partners to fill execution gap. Parallel ecosystem moves in Singapore (SG Semiconductor, A*STAR S$46m lab with 50 company participants) and India (EY-IESA projects 3x market growth to $200B by 2035) signal geographic diversification of packaging competency, but TSMC's Taiwan-centric hub consolidation maintains dominant position at the technical interface.

hbm.executive_summary: HBM supply bottlenecks are reshaping competitive positioning around foundry-memory integration. SK hynix validated HBM5 with TSMC and retains key partner status, while Samsung is scaling HBM4 base-die production at 4nm to shrink foundry losses by ~42% YoY in 2026; HBM is projected to reach 30% of total DRAM capacity by 2027, up from 20% currently, creating decisive leverage at the memory-logic interface for suppliers aligned with leading foundries.
